## 1. Organisation background

BridgeLight Education Trust is a UK-registered international development charity based in Bristol. Since 2016, BridgeLight has worked with district education offices, community-based organisations, parent-teacher associations and girls' clubs in Malawi and Tanzania.

BridgeLight's Malawi country team is based in Zomba, with district coordinators in Machinga and Mangochi. The team has implemented three education access projects since 2018, including the Safe Steps to School pilot in Machinga, which supported 1,480 learners, mostly girls aged 10-17, to return to school after COVID-19 closures.

## 2. Project summary

The Girls Return to Learning and Safety Programme will run for two years in 40 primary and community day secondary schools across Machinga and Mangochi districts. It will support adolescent girls who have dropped out, are irregularly attending, or are at risk of early marriage.

The programme will directly support 1,200 girls and young women aged 10-19, plus 800 caregivers and 160 school and community actors. It will prioritise girls with disabilities, married adolescent girls seeking school re-entry, girls from ultra-poor households, and girls affected by seasonal migration around Lake Malawi.

The total proposed FCDO budget is GBP 1.184m, excluding in-kind school contributions. The finance worksheet attached to the proposal uses the rounded version '£1.18 million'; the full budget submitted to the portal is £1,184,000.

## 3. Problem statement

In the target schools, girls' attendance and transition remain below district averages. District education officials in Machinga reported that pregnancy, unpaid work, poor menstrual health facilities and household inability to meet school-related costs are the main drivers of dropout among girls aged 12-17.

BridgeLight's 2023 assessment in 18 schools found that 44% of girls interviewed had missed at least five school days in the previous month. Teachers reported that girls who miss more than ten days in a term rarely catch up without remedial support.

## 4. Impact, outcome and outputs

Impact statement: Adolescent girls in Machinga and Mangochi complete basic education in safer, more supportive learning environments.

Outcome statement: By September 2026, adolescent girls targeted by the programme demonstrate improved school retention, attendance and learning continuity, with reduced practical and safeguarding barriers to education.

## 5. Output structure and indicators

### Output 1 - Girls re-enter and remain in education

Impact weighting: 35%; Risk rating: Medium

The project will identify girls who are out of school or at risk of dropout and support them through re-entry counselling, bridge learning sessions, attendance monitoring and case follow-up. By the first Annual Review, the latest internal note in the proposal pack says 612 girls had been re-enrolled by 16 September 2025, although district verification was still being cleaned at the time of drafting.

## 6. Activities

School and community identification of out-of-school girls and girls at risk of dropout.

Re-entry counselling and family engagement through mother groups and school committees.

Bridge learning and remedial sessions delivered by trained teachers after school hours.

Rehabilitation of girls latrines, with lockable doors, handwashing points and menstrual disposal where feasible.

Menstrual health supply distribution through trained focal teachers.

Hardship grants and school re-entry kits for girls facing direct cost barriers.

Safeguarding referral mapping with district social welfare officers and headteachers.

Quarterly district learning meetings and short evidence briefs.

The project will start in October 2024 and run until September 2026. The first reporting year is expected to cover October 2024 to September 2025, although the exact Annual Review cut-off may be confirmed by FCDO after contracting.

## 7. Monitoring, evaluation and learning

BridgeLight will use a logframe-based monitoring system. Data sources will include school attendance registers, re-entry club records, caregiver payment lists, WASH completion certificates, meeting attendance sheets, case referral logs and quarterly survey tools.

Monitoring data will be disaggregated by gender, age band and vulnerability category where the indicator relates to individual beneficiaries. For girls, the core age bands will be 6-11, 12-17 and 18-24. Vulnerability categories include disability, ultra-poor household, married/previously married adolescent, orphaned or separated child, and high dropout-risk household.

Output scoring will use the FCDO five-point system at Annual Review. BridgeLight’s MEL Manager will propose initial scores, but final scores should be agreed with the FCDO review team.

## 8. Value for Money

BridgeLight expects the main cost drivers to be school rehabilitation works, hardship grants, district field transport and local partner facilitation. The business case assumes a cost per directly supported girl of approximately £987 over two years, using the £1.184m proposal budget and 1,200 girls.

Economy will be managed through local procurement for rehabilitation works and competitive pricing for learning kits. Efficiency will be monitored through cost per girl re-enrolled, cost per school with completed WASH works, and staff cost as a share of total programme spend. Effectiveness will be reviewed through attendance, re-entry and progression results. Equity will be assessed through the share of support reaching girls with disabilities, girls from ultra-poor households and girls previously out of school.

## 9. Risk and safeguarding

Main risks include school calendar disruption, inflation in construction materials, local political pressure in beneficiary selection, low mobile-money coverage, and safeguarding risks associated with identifying girls affected by early marriage or abuse. BridgeLight will apply child safeguarding procedures, staff code of conduct, community complaints mechanisms and referral pathways through district social welfare offices.
